company.name: SeatGeek
company.shortDescription: SeatGeek operates a mobile-focused ticket platform and search engine that lets fans buy and sell tickets for events.
company.description:
SeatGeek is a ticket search engine that aggregates ticket listings for live sports, concerts, and theater events. Its data engine helps consumers identify various ticket deals.

The site has a feature called ‘Deal Score’ which assigns a 0-100 metric to all listed tickets in order to ascertain the relative value of tickets for a given event or a set of similar events.

SeatGeek also offers consumers an event discovery tool through its Columbus event calendar and Spotify applications, which take into account user preferences and favorite teams and artists in order to generate recommendations of upcoming local events that match a user’s tastes and preferences.

SeatGeek was launched by Jack Groetzinger and Russell D’Souza in 2009 and its operations are headquartered in New York, United States.

aiResearchSummary.text: SeatGeek is researching systems and methods for controlling event tickets and deal quality for event tickets. The work on controlling event tickets focuses on how tickets to events are issued and controlled, while the deal value metric or deal score enables consumers to identify the quality of a ticket listing and directly compare available event tickets of varying quality throughout a venue. Together these efforts center on ticket issuance, access control, and comparative pricing quality for event inventory.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Series E round raised $238,000,000, or 46.66% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.
caveats: Crunchbase reports 14 rounds but provides 10 detailed rows.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $12,245,864 to $1,238,000,000, a 101.1x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 83 (-11 over 90 days) and market heat at 56 (-20).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
caveats: Crunchbase does not expose the complete weighting behind these proprietary scores.
